intro: Isparta, the rose-growing city of south-west Turkey, keeps an old oriental plane that the reader who found it calls the plane of Çınar Street, Plane Tree Street, in the Sülübey quarter of the city centre. A brass plaque from Isparta Municipality on its trunk gives its age as 800 years and records that the city restored it in 2008. The reader photographed the plaque, sent the tree to us and set the pin on the map themselves; look for the brass plate on a pale, patched trunk.
meta_description: The old oriental plane on Çınar Sokak, Isparta: 800 years old by the municipality's plaque, restored by the city in 2008.

trees.name: The Plane of Çınar Sokak

location.address: 144. Cadde, Sülübey Mahallesi, Isparta (the spot the reader who found it marked)

trees.story:
Isparta Municipality has screwed a brass plaque to this plane's trunk, and it gives the tree's age as 800 years. The plaque calls it one of the meaningful witnesses of the city's history and says the municipality restored it on 19 August 2008.

Nobody we have read explains how the 800 was reached, and plaque ages on Turkish planes are usually tradition rather than a ring count, so treat it as the city's figure. The reader who photographed it measured the trunk at about 4 metres round.

The photograph shows what the restoration left. The trunk is pale and patched where old wounds have healed over, it opens into several heavy limbs, and a chain runs between two of them high up to hold the crown together. The reader knows it as the plane of Çınar Street, and çınar is simply Turkish for plane tree.

The reader who sent the photograph also set the pin, in the Sülübey quarter of central Isparta, by hand on the map rather than by a GPS fix, so the trunk may stand a short way off. Look for the brass plaque.
trees.how_to_recognise: A pale, patched oriental plane trunk with a brass Isparta Municipality plaque reading YAŞI: 800 and a chain between the upper limbs.
verified_sources: Isparta Municipality's plaque on the trunk (Platanus orientalis, Doğu Çınarı, age 800, restored 19/08/2008), seen in a reader's photograph through the app, 2026-11-15

trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-15: tipped by a reader in the app as 'Ancient eastern plane tree on Çınar Street', note 'Dates at up to 800 years old', girth 400 cm, one photograph and no coordinates. The photograph shows Isparta Belediyesi's brass plaque: Platanaceae, Platanus orientalis, Türkçe adı Doğu Çınarı, Yaşı 800, 'Tarihimizin anlamlı şahitlerinden olan asırlık Çınar ağacımız Isparta Belediyesi tarafından restore edilmiştir 19/08/2008'. The owner of the ground (the municipality) is the source for species and age. Pin: OSM has one Çınar Sokak in central Isparta (way 127610225, pedestrian, Kafeler, Kutlubey Mahallesi), about 100 m long; pin at its midpoint, approximate. A travel guide (turna.com, search excerpt only, page refused us) mentions an 800-year-old historic plane in Isparta's centre with tea places around it, which fits the café street. Not to be confused with the Sultanbaba plane (also given as about 800, near the Baba Sultan tomb on a road, per an SDU journal search excerpt) or Yalvaç's 825-year plane in another town. Risk: if the reader's 'Çınar Street' is a different street, the pin is wrong; the plaque and café-street fit make this the likeliest reading. The photograph is 906 x 1287, cropped by the sender but a camera photo, not a screenshot. The tree's exact position on the street is not confirmed. 2026-11-17: the same account that sent the tree moved the pin 892 m south-south-east, from the middle of Çınar Sokak (Kafeler, Kutlubey) to 37.757915, 30.556699 on 144. Cadde in Sülübey Mahallesi (Nominatim reverse). A tree its own finder placed: their move taken, still approximate (a hand-placed pin, no GPS fix). The Kafeler café-street reading was our guess from the street name and is dropped from the page: address, access, story, intro, question texts and FAQ now say only what the plaque and the reader give.

question_meta: The old oriental plane on Çınar Sokak in Isparta: 800 years by the municipality's plaque, restored in 2008. Where to find it.
question_answer: Isparta's old plane on Çınar Sokak is an oriental plane that Isparta Municipality's plaque dates to 800 years. The city restored it on 19 August 2008. It stands in the Sülübey quarter of central Isparta, free to visit.
question_context: The tree is known to us from a reader's photograph of the brass plaque Isparta Municipality fixed to its trunk. The plaque names it Platanus orientalis, the doğu çınarı or eastern plane, gives its age as 800, calls it one of the meaningful witnesses of the city's history and records a restoration by the municipality on 19 August 2008. How the age was reached is not stated, so it is the city's figure rather than a measurement. The reader measured the trunk at about 4 metres round. A chain between the upper limbs helps hold the crown together. The reader knows it as the plane of Çınar Street, and çınar simply means plane tree. The pin is where that reader placed it on the map, in the Sülübey quarter of central Isparta; it was set by hand rather than by a GPS fix at the trunk, so the tree may stand a short way off, and the plaque is the surest way to know it. Isparta has other old planes with large ages attached, among them the Sultanbaba plane and the plane at Yalvaç, so this page covers only the one with the municipality's plaque reading 800.

faq.q: How old is the plane on Çınar Sokak?
faq.a: 800 years, by the plaque Isparta Municipality fixed to its trunk. How that figure was reached is not stated.
On 19 August 2008, by Isparta Municipality, according to the same plaque.
In the Sülübey quarter of central Isparta, where the reader who found it placed the pin. Look for the brass plaque.
